title: A reference to const
note: A const reference accepts variables and temporary values. A non-const lvalue reference cannot bind to a literal.

note: Pass addresses with & and access the pointed-to values with *. This function requires two valid, non-null pointers.

note: The argument types and number of arguments select the overload. The f suffix makes 2.5f a float.

title: Default arguments
note: Default values fill in omitted trailing arguments. The first argument is still required.

note: The recursive call must move toward the base case. Printing after the recursive call produces ascending order.

title: Const data and const pointers
note: const int* protects data through the pointer; int* const protects the pointer itself.

title: Scope, shadowing, and static locals
note: A local name can shadow a global name. ::x selects global x. A static local is initialized once and retains its value between calls.

note: Run this after predicting the output. Each object has its own x and y values. The same member functions operate on the object named to the left of the dot.

note: An invariant is a rule that should remain true for every valid object. Here grade always stays in [0,100]. Invalid updates return false and preserve the previous value. An invalid initial grade leaves the fallback grade of 0.

note: Private coordinates are accessed through a public interface. Queries are const; const references avoid unnecessary copies.

note: A complete solution to your array exercise. The function requires a nonempty array and chooses the first point when distances tie.

title: Temperature: const members and unit conversion
note: A const scale is initialized in the initializer list. Absolute readings use the 32-degree offset; temperature differences do not. An 18°F increase is a 10°C increase.

title: Box: const objects and shared static members
note: Static data belongs to the class. Constructors increase the live-object count, and the destructor decreases it. A const method can modify static data, but that does not make arbitrary counter changes meaningful.

title: Line: composition with two Points
note: A Line has two Point objects. Member objects are constructed in declaration order before the constructor body, regardless of initializer-list order.

title: Nodes and a linked chain
note: next is a pointer, not a nested Node object. The stack objects own their own lifetimes; these links do not allocate or own nodes.

title: Dynamic arrays and dynamic objects
note: Match new with delete and new[] with delete[]. Do not overwrite the only owning pointer before releasing its allocation. Never delete an address of a local variable.

title: Student: owning a dynamic grade array
note: An owning raw pointer needs destruction and independent copies. This Rule of Three example initializes grades, validates input, and implements copy construction and copy assignment. In production, prefer std::vector for Rule of Zero ownership.

title: A friend function of two classes
note: The forward declaration makes ClassB known. Friendship grants this specific function access; it does not make the function a member.

title: A friend class
note: Every member of B can access A’s private data. Friendship is neither reciprocal, transitive, nor inherited.

title: One friend member function
note: TWO must declare print before ONE can name it as a friend. Granting one method friendship is narrower than granting the entire class.

title: this: returning a copy or a reference
note: Returning *this by value creates an independent result. Returning it by reference aliases the original object. A returned reference must not outlive the object.

note: An UnderGrad is a Student. Private base data still exists in the base subobject but is not directly accessible to the derived class. Construction runs base first; destruction runs derived first.

title: Checked downcasting with dynamic_cast
note: Upcasting a pointer or reference preserves the original object. Copying a derived object into a base object can slice it. A failed pointer dynamic_cast returns nullptr; a failed reference cast throws std::bad_cast.

title: Student: comparison, +=, and stream output
note: Return Student& from += to permit chaining. Stream operators return their stream. Grade equality here is exact and appropriate for these integer-valued demonstration grades.

title: Point: unary and binary operators
note: Unary minus returns a new Point; binary subtraction uses both operands. Equality should return bool. Exact coordinate equality is demonstrated here; approximate comparisons may be needed for calculated floating-point values.
